items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The schools in, I think, Houston, where Roy Hargrove – there’s a performing arts school.

ctx.x: Yeah, audition tapes. Based on those tapes, they’ll be asked to come in for a live audition. Very few of those made it past that pre-audition screening. These are students who are – we’re talking about masters students. But a lot of them were also high school, and you could hear the deficiencies, especially when you’re talking about coming to a school on that level, Juilliard, because right away you’re expected to participate. First of all, everybody has to participate in ensemble. That’s a must. You have to…

Ben Riley put it perfect, talking about the young people who – they have great technique, but they can’t tell a story yet. Ben Riley said, “Yeah, well, they haven’t had their hearts broken yet.” It was well put. That’s when they will be able to have something to talk about. They have something to say when they have their hearts broken, when they live life, essentially.
